gaps.cause: different basis (budgetary schedules vs GAAP statement)
gaps.explanation: Re-read pp5, 10-22. Nothing printed is missing and nothing is counted twice: each governmental fund is in detail once, from its budgetary-basis schedule (General p10; nonmajor special revenue pp14-20; Debt Service p21; Street Projects and Miscellaneous Projects p22), and the South Sioux City Community Foundation (no budget schedule) from its GAAP combining column p12 (44,961). Statement p5 (GAAP): General 10,532,137 + Street Projects 3,294,595 + Other Governmental Funds 8,529,845 = 22,356,577 (JSON receipts total matches the page). Detail 22,860,345, schedule above by 503,768, per fund (budget actual vs GAAP column): General 10,815,183 (p10) vs 10,532,137 = +283,046; Street Projects 3,398,614 (p22) vs 3,294,595 = +104,019; nonmajor funds whose GAAP column is in the trim (pp11-13): W 29th & Hwy 77 TIF 622,538 vs 564,632 = +57,906 (budget prints Intergovernmental 77,508 the GAAP column does not); Riverview HCI Flatwater TIF 294,323 vs 217,634 = +76,689; Police Pension 235,763 vs 234,469 = +1,294; Wireless 911 81,808 vs 75,341 = +6,467; Economic Development Sales Tax 269,187 vs 155,140 = +114,047; Public Safety Sales Tax 714,185 vs 729,796 = -15,611; Northeast Redevelopment Area TIF 583,128 vs 592,499 = -9,371; Community Foundation 44,961 = 44,961; Harvest Meadows, Marina Inn, Misc Projects 0 = 0. The other nine nonmajor funds (Capital Improvement Sales Tax 2,739,389, Library 850,403, Fire 963,924, All America City TIF 15,059, County/LEC Sales Tax 21,630, Opioids Settlement 10,067, W 25th - W 39th TIF 229,631, Roth TIF 613,428, Debt Service 357,124; budget total 5,800,655) have their GAAP columns on the first nonmajor combining page (report p75, 'Combining Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances - Governmental Nonmajor Funds'; page not in trim, trimmed p11 is report p76 '(Continued)'); their GAAP total is 8,529,845 - 2,614,472 (visible columns) = 5,915,373, so -114,718. 283,046 + 104,019 + 231,421 - 114,718 = 503,768 = the gap. Both sides are printed; no line to add or remove.

Note (other financing, not this gap row): detail 95 'Transfer out (inside Public Safety)' -1,816,062 (p12 GAAP Harvest Meadows column) is the same money as detail 94 (p20 Public Safety 1,816,062); pass 4 kept both as printed so that governmental transfers out tie to p5 (4,641,145). gaps.cause: different basis (budgetary sale proceeds counted in the check; not debt)
gaps.explanation: All printed debt proceeds are in detail once: p5 Inception of Lease 140,707 (JSON debt_proceeds) = General 32,966 (detail 18, p10 'Proceeds from Issuance of Lease') + Other Governmental Funds 107,741 (detail 28, p14 Capital Improvement Sales Tax 'Issuance of Lease'; the p13 GAAP Total column prints the same 107,741 as 'Payment to Refunded Bond Escrow Agent'). Schedule 243,171 = 140,707 + detail 49 All America City TIF 'Proceeds from Sale of Uncapitalized Assets' 102,464 (p15 budget schedule), a sale, not debt. The GAAP statement prints the nonmajor sale as 'Proceeds from Sale of Land Held for Resale' 35,606 (p5; p13 'Proceeds from Sale of Captial Assets' 35,606; JSON other_financing); no other nonmajor budget schedule prints a sale row, so 102,464 (budgetary) vs 35,606 (GAAP, fund column on report p75, page not in trim) is the same sale on two bases. debt_proceeds + other_financing 176,313 vs detail 243,171: difference 66,858 = 102,464 - 35,606. Adding the 35,606 GAAP row would count the sale twice; nothing to add or remove.
